title: Economic Data Watch
question: Is this a new release, a revised value, or a change in what the data measure?
description: Follow selected official release plans and source versions, while separating reference periods, publication dates and observed availability.

coverage.label: countries in the current monitoring panel
verified new-release event in the follow-up

preview_scope: Seven historical cases across five countries, plus one verified Vietnam release observed on 3 November 2026. Historical examples are distinct from the four-country current panel.
insight: Vietnam’s October CPI value of 5.09% is a new reference month, not a revision of September’s 5.08%.
limitations: The current panel is selected coverage, not exhaustive global monitoring.
The follow-up establishes one new release and no verified same-period numeric revisions; this is not a lifetime count.
Capture time establishes observation, not first public availability; date-only release plans do not establish intraday delays.
Historical examples preserve limits such as archived homepage text, inaccessible full releases and unresolved first-access times.

records.title: Brazil: a census postponement is a plan change
records.summary: An archived IBGE English homepage records an announcement dated 17 March 2020 that moves the planned 2020 census to 2021. This case records that contemporary plan change, not the eventual completion year.

records.title: Japan: survey forms can affect year-on-year comparability
records.summary: Japan’s Statistics Bureau explains on 9 March 2018 that half the household sample began using new diary forms in January. It warns of possible discontinuity in year-on-year changes and contributions, supplies a propensity-score/inverse-probability adjustment, and records a retrospective recalculation on 8 February 2019.

title: India Deposit Rate Monitor
question: Which deposit quotes are comparable, and what does each date actually establish?
description: Research selected historical bank rate tables with customer, amount and tenor context attached to every quote.
preview_scope: Three selected cases. The full edition contains 254 candidates and selected domestic retail INR deposit buckets covering a nominal 365-day point, plus 12 historical RBI policy-rate points.
insight: An Axis rate-card filename says 8 June, but the selected retail table states 18 May; both differ from the archive observation date.
limitations: The 188 accepted observations include repeat captures; they are not 188 distinct rate changes.
The scope is general-public domestic retail INR deposits; original tenor labels and amount thresholds remain authoritative.
Sparse archives do not identify the first adjustment or prove that a dated PDF quote was active on its capture date.
Comparisons are descriptive; causal monetary-policy pass-through, personalized returns and investment recommendations are outside scope.

title: Curriculum Observatory
question: What changed in a degree’s requirements, course content or approved options?
description: Compare official curriculum versions with course-level evidence, conditions and document timing kept together.
preview_scope: 13 selected cases from six universities. Full-edition counts describe the underlying research, not the size of this public sample.
insight: A course can gain a completion role without being newly created; a listed option can also carry a non-delivery notice.
limitations: Selected official programme and course texts, not a census of all courses at these institutions.
Five institutions have five observed annual editions; MIT’s 2025/26 central annual programme rules remain a documented gap.
Catalogue wording and eligibility do not measure teaching, student uptake or learning outcomes.
Academic-year versions, entry cohorts and retrieval dates are distinct; credits stay in each institution’s own units.

title: Drug Recovery Watch
question: How do recovery expectations differ from delivery dates, supply notes and observed outcomes?
description: Track a fixed set of FDA-source product presentations across saved observations, preserving identity holds, date precision and conflicting supply statements.

coverage.label: substantive revisions in the observed pair

preview_scope: Five selected interpretation cases, including one held identity. The underlying observations were captured on 2 and 3 November 2026; API source versions were 30 October and 2 November.
insight: A November delivery estimate and a September-next-year recovery estimate can coexist in the same product record.
limitations: The 107 accepted records form a frozen cohort; they do not represent all US shortages or individual medicines.
Across this one observation pair, 94 raw records were identical and 13 differed only in annotation-array order; no substantive forecast or supply-field changes were found.
Three identity conflicts remain outside the accepted cohort; one accepted record retains a supply conflict that blocks recovery-outcome interpretation.
No real-world inventory validation, recovery rate, forecast accuracy or final recovery outcome is reported. Current API links may differ from saved historical evidence.

title: Policy Target Watch
question: What did a government originally target, what changed, and which progress comparisons remain valid?
description: Link national Digital Decade targets to revised roadmaps and official progress measures, with deadlines and definitions visible.
preview_scope: Six selected cases. The full edition contains 34 accepted and 5 held records: 2 numeric adjustments, 22 added targets and 10 unchanged targets among the accepted records.
insight: Austria’s skills target moves down and Finland’s SME target moves up; equal percentages elsewhere can still hide a definition change.
limitations: Selected national roadmaps and progress reports; no comprehensive EU-country ranking.
National targets, EU collective targets, planned annual trajectories and observed results remain separate.
Numeric comparison depends on aligned scope and definition. An added target is not a zero-to-target increase.
All selected 2030 deadlines are still ahead. Current gaps do not establish final delivery, causes or political motives.

records.title: Austria lowers the national basic digital skills target
records.period: Original and revised roadmap versions; 2025 progress reported in 2026
records.summary: Austria’s original roadmap uses a maximum-100% formulation and also contains a generic 80% heading. The Commission’s 2024 assessment identifies the national target as 100%. The revised roadmap sets 80% for 2030, supporting a 20-percentage-point reduction with the original qualifier retained.

title: Synopsis Notes
question: Which character, livelihood and story details do two language versions actually state?
description: An exploratory comparison of official English and French film introductions, with shared facts, information differences and unresolved interpretations kept visible.

coverage.label: films in the fixed selection frame
selected cases in this public preview

preview_scope: Seven selected cases from a fresh factual review of 29 complete pairs within the 38-film Un Certain Regard selections for 2022 and 2024. All seven public cases have two readable, hash-verified saved snapshots. Selection years are not capture dates: pages were retrieved in November 2026.
insight: Differences can be concrete, such as a named family relationship or job, while some pairs preserve the same facts and some wording requires interpretation.
limitations: This is an exploratory text comparison, not a cultural trend index or a translation-quality score.
Nine of the 38 frame entries lack a complete bounded English/French pair and remain unclassified.

The review reads all 29 preserved text pairs. Of their 58 full-page snapshot files, 42 were locally readable and reverified; 16 were not resident and were skipped. Every public case has both full snapshots verified.
The snapshots are saved web-tool text extractions, not original HTML. They were retrieved in November 2026; first publication dates, translation direction and past wording are unknown.
A detail not stated in an introduction may still appear in the film. No film-level fact checking or inference about editorial motives is made.
The case review was performed by AI agents, not certified by a human bilingual editor.
